messages:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — proposing a cohort-pruning + fast-fail protocol for the EU->US staged rollout. Goal: reduce BLAST of traffic when model variant regresses. Sketch below.

Omar Chen: SG. What's the target SLO we want to protect? 95th p50 or p99 latency? error rate?

Maya Patel: Primary guard = 99th latency <= 250ms and model error (regressions on key prompts) < 1% at cohort level. If either fails we prune cohorts by 50% every 5m until stable.

Liam O'Neill: How do we pick cohorts? random sampling or tenant-aware? My vote: weight by recent qps and include a holdback group of 5% for rollback signals.

Sophia Garcia: Customer asks: Enterprise customers want immediate opt-out. Need per-tenant kill-switch + per-region emergency flag. Also need a clear launch gate for GA :
- 72h no critical regressions in top 5 customers
- Automated quality checks (prompt set) pass

Maya Patel: Proposed concrete rules:
1) Start at 1% global (EU) -> ramp to 10% in 4 steps
2) During ramp, run continuous A/B evaluation against control with rolling window 30m
3) If regression delta > 0.8% on primary eval set OR 99th latency > 250ms for 2 windows -> trigger prune
4) Prune algorithm: remove worst-performing 50% of cohorts by error delta; if unexplained, fallback to model-stable variant

Jen (devex-bot): Checklist created: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/1715439999

Omar Chen: Need implementation detail for prune: is it by user-id hash ranges? by tenant buckets? We should avoid correlated failure modes.

Liam O'Neill: Hash-based cohorts with salt + tenant override list. E.g.
```
flag: cohort_salt=0x9f
cohort = hash(user_id + salt) % 100
```
Then prune by cohort id ranges.

Sophia Garcia: Also add a circuit-breaker: if 3 consecutive prunes occur within 1h, auto-fallback full traffic to control and page oncall.

Maya Patel: Ops runbook snippet:
- On prune alert: run quick sanity eval on 200 diverse prompts (script: /ops/eval/fast_check.sh)
- If sanity passes -> continue ramp; if fails -> rollback and notify customers

Liam O'Neill: Small UX note: flagging the cohorts in Console with human-readable names and a "undo" for last prune would help SREs.

Sophia Garcia: Launch gating final ask: require infra green (no GPU throttling), telemetry pipeline healthy (no 50% telemetry drop), and at least one customer signed off on opt-in test.

Maya Patel: Ok I'll draft the feature flag config and run it by eng-sre. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

prod-bot: Deploy scheduled: rollout-controller v2 -> canary job queued (id: rc-5823)

Omar Chen: tagging @Liam O'Neill for cohort code review, and @Sophia Garcia for customer comms review

Liam O'Neill: I'll open a PR today with hash-salt impl and tests.

Sophia Garcia: I'll prepare a one-pager for customers and a quick opt-out FAQ.
